prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop landing and documentation homepage comp, 1536×1024 landscape
Primary request: design a shippable Atlas documentation site for a composable Bun/TypeScript library. Greek mythology interpreted through a confident 1980s scientific-terminal lens.
Structure: a thin utility strip at top; compact left-aligned brand/navigation; first viewport split 58/42. On the left, a huge typographic ATLAS title, compact product statement, two clear actions, the exact install command "bun add @wess/atlas", and a concise code sample. On the right, a monumental code-native-looking line illustration of Atlas holding a wireframe celestial sphere, integrated into a coordinate grid. Show the start of a package index below the fold so this unmistakably reads as a documentation website.
Subject/content: real product facts only — "Composable, functional Bun/TypeScript building blocks", "19 packages", "Bun-native", "No classes", navigation labels "GUIDES", "PACKAGES", "API", "GITHUB".
Style/medium: polished responsive web UI mockup, not a poster and not a photograph. An archaeological field terminal from 1986: deep Aegean navy ground, electric cyan survey lines, one magenta registration accent, warm limestone text, sparse Greek-key rules, halftone celestial map, crisp technical labels. Monumental but highly readable.
Typography: wide geometric uppercase display with chiseled proportions for ATLAS, pragmatic humanist sans for reading, condensed mono for technical labels and code.
Composition/framing: full browser viewport, precise UI chrome and real content hierarchy, generous asymmetry, one dominant Atlas-and-orb move, quiet supporting regions.
Lighting/mood: phosphor glow against midnight Aegean blue; no glassmorphism.
Constraints: no rounded bento cards, no generic SaaS gradient blobs, no tiny unreadable fake paragraphs, no columns used as decorative clipart, no gold luxury aesthetic, no invented metrics or customers, no logos other than the word ATLAS, no watermark.
